posts.title: Cultural Appropriation Controversies: Timeline
posts.script: I wasn't supposed to share this, but the cultural appropriation controversies timeline explained reveals how messy internet outrage really is. Quick context: from pop stars to local bakeries, borrowing culture has always sparked fierce debate. Back in November 2004, Gwen Stefani dropped her Harajuku Girls track, then Margaret Cho called out the racial stereotypes in October 2005. Katy Perry faced massive backlash at the 2013 American Music Awards for dressing as a geisha, but that was just the start. June 2019 rolled around and Kim Kardashian reportedly faced fierce pushback after naming her shapewear line Kimono. Justin Bieber then drew an online firestorm in 2021 for wearing blonde dreadlocks, so Awkwafina finally addressed her past blaccent accusations in 2022. But one date doesn't add up. August 28, 2026 brought a wild twist when an Edmonton bakery owner posted a response video over a bánh mì croissant. Private messages went viral the next day, sparking heated debates about representation. So whose side are you on? Full dated timeline on GenZHype dot com.
